title: Porosity modulation of activated ZIF-templated carbons via compaction for hydrogen and CO2 storage applications
material_description: AC-BF900 | activated ZIF-templated carbon: ZIF-8 template (Basolite Z1200, Sigma-Aldrich; degassed 200 C, 3 h) soaked in furfuryl alcohol (liquid impregnation, LI), FA polymerised under Ar at 80 C for 24 h and 150 C for 6 h, carbonised under Ar at 900 C for 8 h (BF900); KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4, 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min; not compacted
purification_method: washed three times with 2 M HCl at room temperature, then with distilled water to neutral pH; dried at 120 C for 3 h
activation_method: KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4, 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min
source_location: main article page 6 (p. 10965), Fig. 5a, series AC-BF900 (black triangles)
notes: archive: Fig5a_AC-BF900.json; marker 0 of the archive (pixel 385.5, 1009.0). Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), stored as 77.15 K; pressure basis (absolute or gauge) not stated. Fig. 5 is titled "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); gravimetric, buoyancy-corrected (carbon density 1.5-1.8 g cm-3, hydrogen density 0.04 g cm-3), so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default. BET range: 0.06-0.22. Table 1 surface area is BET (N2, -196 C); values in parentheses are micropore surface area and micropore volume (method not stated); total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other = single point). NLDFT pore-size maxima 6/12/25 A (0.6/1.2/2.5 nm), not stored as one diameter. Degassed at 200 C and 10^-10 bar (= 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h after oven drying at 80 C for 24 h; duration range not stored as a number. packing density 0.4 g cm-3 (as printed; determined after compaction under a mild load of 1 tonne (74 MPa) for 10 min in a 1.3 cm die, or from rho_d = (1/rho_s + V_T)^-1).
basis_evidence: Fig. 5 caption: "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); Section 2.3: "The hydrogen uptake was corrected for buoyancy effects with a carbon density of 1.5-1.8 g cm-3 and a hydrogen density of 0.04 g cm-3"

purification_method: washed three times with 2 M HCl at room temperature, then with distilled water to neutral pH; dried at 120 C for 3 h
activation_method: KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4, 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min
source_location: main article page 6 (p. 10965), Fig. 5c, series AC-CB700 (black triangles)
notes: archive: Fig5c_AC-CB700.json; marker 17 of the archive (pixel 908.0, 954.7). Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), stored as 77.15 K; pressure basis (absolute or gauge) not stated. Fig. 5 is titled "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); gravimetric, buoyancy-corrected (carbon density 1.5-1.8 g cm-3, hydrogen density 0.04 g cm-3), so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default. BET range: 0.06-0.22. Table 1 surface area is BET (N2, -196 C); values in parentheses are micropore surface area and micropore volume (method not stated); total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other = single point). NLDFT pore-size maxima 8/12/21 A (0.8/1.2/2.1 nm), not stored as one diameter. Degassed at 200 C and 10^-10 bar (= 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h after oven drying at 80 C for 24 h; duration range not stored as a number. packing density 0.45 g cm-3 (as printed; determined after compaction under a mild load of 1 tonne (74 MPa) for 10 min in a 1.3 cm die, or from rho_d = (1/rho_s + V_T)^-1).
basis_evidence: Fig. 5 caption: "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); Section 2.3: "The hydrogen uptake was corrected for buoyancy effects with a carbon density of 1.5-1.8 g cm-3 and a hydrogen density of 0.04 g cm-3"

purification_method: washed three times with 2 M HCl at room temperature, then with distilled water to neutral pH; dried at 120 C for 3 h
activation_method: KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4, 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min
source_location: main article page 6 (p. 10965), Fig. 5d, series AC-CB850 (black triangles)
notes: archive: Fig5d_AC-CB850.json; marker 18 of the archive (pixel 848.0, 1275.3). Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), stored as 77.15 K; pressure basis (absolute or gauge) not stated. Fig. 5 is titled "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); gravimetric, buoyancy-corrected (carbon density 1.5-1.8 g cm-3, hydrogen density 0.04 g cm-3), so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default. BET range: 0.06-0.22. Table 1 surface area is BET (N2, -196 C); values in parentheses are micropore surface area and micropore volume (method not stated); total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other = single point). NLDFT pore-size maxima 8/12/21 A (0.8/1.2/2.1 nm), not stored as one diameter. Degassed at 200 C and 10^-10 bar (= 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h after oven drying at 80 C for 24 h; duration range not stored as a number. packing density 0.52 g cm-3 (as printed; determined after compaction under a mild load of 1 tonne (74 MPa) for 10 min in a 1.3 cm die, or from rho_d = (1/rho_s + V_T)^-1).
basis_evidence: Fig. 5 caption: "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); Section 2.3: "The hydrogen uptake was corrected for buoyancy effects with a carbon density of 1.5-1.8 g cm-3 and a hydrogen density of 0.04 g cm-3"

purification_method: washed three times with 2 M HCl at room temperature, then with distilled water to neutral pH; dried at 120 C for 3 h
activation_method: KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4, 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min
source_location: main article page 6 (p. 10965), Fig. 5a, series AC-BF900@10Ton (blue triangles)
notes: archive: Fig5a_AC-BF900at10Ton.json; marker 3 of the archive (pixel 314.3, 1093.4). this blob is two overlapping markers of the same colour (the series is drawn as two near-coincident curves, offset about 2-4 px); not separable, centroid of the pair recorded. Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), stored as 77.15 K; pressure basis (absolute or gauge) not stated. Fig. 5 is titled "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); gravimetric, buoyancy-corrected (carbon density 1.5-1.8 g cm-3, hydrogen density 0.04 g cm-3), so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default. BET range: 0.06-0.22. Table 1 surface area is BET (N2, -196 C); values in parentheses are micropore surface area and micropore volume (method not stated); total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other = single point). NLDFT pore-size maxima 6/12/23 A (0.6/1.2/2.3 nm), not stored as one diameter. Degassed at 200 C and 10^-10 bar (= 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h after oven drying at 80 C for 24 h; duration range not stored as a number. packing density printed as ca. 0.68 g cm-3 for all samples compacted at 10 tonnes.
basis_evidence: Fig. 5 caption: "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); Section 2.3: "The hydrogen uptake was corrected for buoyancy effects with a carbon density of 1.5-1.8 g cm-3 and a hydrogen density of 0.04 g cm-3"

purification_method: washed three times with 2 M HCl at room temperature, then with distilled water to neutral pH; dried at 120 C for 3 h
activation_method: KOH activation: carbon/KOH weight ratio 1/4, 700 C for 1 h under N2 flow, ramp 3 C/min
source_location: main article page 6 (p. 10965), Fig. 5b, series AC-BF1000@10Ton (blue triangles)
notes: archive: Fig5b_AC-BF1000at10Ton.json; marker 16 of the archive (pixel 490.0, 1279.7). Temperature printed as -196 C (liquid nitrogen bath), stored as 77.15 K; pressure basis (absolute or gauge) not stated. Fig. 5 is titled "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); gravimetric, buoyancy-corrected (carbon density 1.5-1.8 g cm-3, hydrogen density 0.04 g cm-3), so basis_inferred = excess by the instrumental default. BET range: 0.06-0.22. Table 1 surface area is BET (N2, -196 C); values in parentheses are micropore surface area and micropore volume (method not stated); total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 = 0.99 (pore_volume_method other = single point). NLDFT pore-size maxima 9/13/21 A (0.9/1.3/2.1 nm), not stored as one diameter. Degassed at 200 C and 10^-10 bar (= 1e-05 Pa) for 4-6 h after oven drying at 80 C for 24 h; duration range not stored as a number. packing density printed as ca. 0.68 g cm-3 for all samples compacted at 10 tonnes.
basis_evidence: Fig. 5 caption: "Total hydrogen uptake capacity" (total not defined); Section 2.3: "The hydrogen uptake was corrected for buoyancy effects with a carbon density of 1.5-1.8 g cm-3 and a hydrogen density of 0.04 g cm-3"
